messages:
alex: Heads up — CI job started failing intermittently when the test matrix runs two containers that both call `redwoodctl login --headless --profile ci`. One container pauses for ~8-12s with no output and then proceeds.

rina: I reproduced locally with a tiny docker-compose setup. When both processes target the same profile they race on the token cache.

chris: Sample repro I used:
```
# shell A
redwoodctl login --headless --profile ci &
# shell B
redwoodctl login --headless --profile ci &
wait
```
Shell B hangs, no browser url printed.

alex: Hung process log snippet:
```
INFO auth: start headless login
WARN auth: cache lock active, waiting
DEBUG auth: sleeping 250ms
ERROR auth: token refresh canceled
```
No interactive prompt, and the runner shows zero network calls until it unsticks.

rina: Workaround: serialize login (single login step before tests) or create a token ahead of time: `redwoodctl token create --profile ci` in your entrypoint. Not ideal for parallel job speed.

chris: Root cause seems to be the lock strategy: current CLI uses mkdir/marker files under `~/.redwoodctl` which doesn't behave atomically on some overlayfs/NFS setups. If two processes create the same marker it leads to races.

alex: Proposed fixes: switch to POSIX advisory fcntl locks where available, and fallback to an atomic rename approach. Also add an explicit flag for ephemeral CI: `--skip-token-cache`.

rina: I noticed another oddity: `REDWOODCTL_PROFILE` env var is inconsistently respected by `login --headless`. Our Dockerfile set the env but `login` ignored it unless `--profile` was passed. Could be an argument parsing path.

chris: I pushed a draft PR with fcntl locking + exponential backoff + `--skip-token-cache` opt-out: gh:redwood/cli#472 (draft). On my linux runner the races disappeared. I left a note about WSL and older kernel overlayfs edgecases.

alex: Can we add `--skip-token-cache` to CI images as the default for ephemeral runners? Or at least a recommended snippet for docker-entrypoint? Something like:
```
#!/bin/sh
set -e
: ${REDWOODCTL_PROFILE:=ci}
redwoodctl token create --profile "$REDWOODCTL_PROFILE" || true
exec "$@"
```
That pre-seeds a token and avoids the race without changing test code.

rina: Also filed a separate issue about aggressive immediate retries when token refresh fails — the client retried 3 times with zero backoff which skewed auth metrics. We should add jitter/backoff.

infra-bot: CI report: gh:redwood/cli#472 linux-amd64 unit tests passed :white_check_mark: (artifact: logs/472/summary.txt).

alex: Thanks. Once PR lands can someone add a short note in devex docs about: 1) profile precedence (env vs flag), 2) skipping token cache in ephemeral runners, and 3) the docker-entrypoint snippet? I'll update our internal image recipes.

chris: Yep I'll add docs + a small test in our CI matrix to ensure `login --headless` honors `REDWOODCTL_PROFILE` going forward. If you hit post-merge flakiness ping me with runner type and raw logs.

alex: Leaving here for triage. If anyone sees the stall after merge, @chris please collect strace and runner FS type.
